claim: Moving part of a task's rules or state into an external, well-structured display lowers errors, steps and time for humans (Zhang & Norman 1994, N=18-36 per experiment). A modern Tower of Hanoi replication found the gain was in completion, not move quality.
agent_test: Run the same task with state held in a persistent structured file versus held in context only, at equal tokens; compare error and step counts.

claim: Hutchins's cockpit case: a memory task is done by a whole system of card, booklet, spoken callouts and speed bugs; redundancy across media lets the crew catch errors. Evidence is ethnographic, with no effect sizes.
agent_test: Give the agent two redundant representations of one intermediate result (table and prose) and measure whether mismatch checks catch injected errors.

claim: Epistemic actions (acting on the world to simplify thought) are cheaper than mental computation: Tetris physical rotation about 100 ms versus about 800-1200 ms mental (pilot estimate), and players rotate more than needed.
schema_part: O (act-to-learn operator, e.g. run code or probe instead of reasoning)
agent_test: Compare an agent that probes with a tool before committing to one that reasons only, on tasks where a cheap probe exists, at equal tokens.

claim: Multi-agent debate beat single agent, reflection and majority vote in the founding study (arithmetic 81.8 vs 67.0; GSM8K 85.0 vs 77.0; 3 agents, 2 rounds, ChatGPT; verified against the paper).
agent_test: Replicate with matched total tokens against self-consistency; see K05.

claim: Under matched compute, multi-agent debate rarely beats chain of thought or self-consistency: no method wins more than 20% of 36 settings, about 15% for four of five methods; Smit et al. also found debate not reliably better. Gap search: Choi 2025 (Qwen2.5-7B, 5 agents) finds majority voting 0.7691 beats debate T=2/3/5 (0.7377/0.7112/0.7050) and single agent 0.7205; Smit 2024 agrees. Untested on frontier models and with an external verifier.
schema_part: none (do not add a debate operator; keep single agent plus verifier)
agent_test: Debate versus self-consistency at equal tokens on our own benchmarks.

claim: Mixing different models in debate helps where mixing copies of one model does not (Heter-SoM +6.4%, Heter-EoT +8.2% over averages), but Self-MoA found repeated samples of the single best model beat mixed models (+6.6% on AlpacaEval 2.0). The two results conflict. Gap search: Self-MoA 65.7 vs mixed-MoA 59.1 on AlpacaEval 2.0 (quality coefficient above diversity, R2 about 0.7); AgentNet BBH (N=100) is mixed (3 agents homogeneous 0.86 vs 0.81 hetero; 5 agents 0.79 vs 0.85). No study matches tokens across both; stays contested, leaning to resample the best model.
agent_test: Compare sampling one strong model N times against mixing weaker models at equal tokens.

claim: More agents by plain sampling and voting raises accuracy, more on harder tasks (GSM8K +12 to +24 points); a 13B model with 15 samples reached 59% versus 54% for 70B.
agent_test: Already a baseline arm; measure marginal gain per token versus the scaffold.

claim: Self-correction without an external label does not help and can hurt: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one round; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over two rounds (verified). Gap search: Tyen 2024 shows the bottleneck is finding the error (GPT-4 52.87 on locating it), not fixing it; true-location backtracking gives +18 to +44 points on wrong traces versus +5 to +22 with random location; CRITIC with a tool beats CRITIC without tool (HotpotQA F1 50.5 vs 46.1, CoT 46.1).
schema_part: G (verifier must use external evidence, not self-opinion)
agent_test: Compare self-review against review with a tool check or test oracle at equal tokens. Give the verifier output as a step location, not a yes/no.

claim: Multi-agent systems fail mostly through design and coordination: 41% to 86.7% failure across 7 systems; clusters system design 41.8%, inter-agent misalignment 36.9%, verification 21.3%. Fixes gave modest gains (+9.4% roles, +15.6% verifier on ChatDev ProgramDev). Same paper, three evidence copies.
agent_test: Add a task-objective verifier stage to the loop and measure success at equal tokens.

claim: Whether more agents help depends on the task: across 260 configurations, +80.8% (decomposable finance, centralized) to -70.0% (sequential planning); all multi-agent variants hurt planning; gains vanish when a single agent already exceeds about 45% (verified; error amplification 17.2 independent vs 4.4 centralized). Gap search: Kim's model picks the best architecture in 87% of held-out configurations (cross-validated R2 0.373; capability-only 54%), with a rule of thumb that agents stop helping once the single-agent score passes about 0.45; but its coordination predictors are measured from traces, so it is not a pre-run predictor. Decomposability (Finance 0.41, +80.8%) versus strict sequence (PlanCraft, -70%) carries the sign.
schema_part: none (single agent default; decompose only when subtasks are independent)
agent_test: Test decomposition only on parallelizable items; keep sequential items single-thread.

claim: Changing the interface between model and computer matters: SWE-agent's custom interface solved 18.0% of SWE-bench Lite versus 11.0% for shell-only (same GPT-4 Turbo, 64% relative, +7.0 points); removing the linter cost 3 points. Gap search: ablations on Lite (GPT-4 Turbo): no edit action 10.3, edit without linting 15.0, with linting 18.0; window 30 lines 14.3, 100 lines 18.0, whole file 12.7; HumanEvalFix 87.7/89.7/87.9 (Python/JS/Java), so the 87.7 versus 88.3 mismatch is a text/table aggregation difference. A bash-only agent is now claimed above 74% on SWE-bench Verified (README only), so the interface gain is probably smaller for current models; not tested outside code.
agent_test: Ablate observation format (windowed view, linter feedback) on our tool loop at equal tokens.

claim: Externalised memory helps agents: Generative Agents ablation (full 29.89 vs no memory/planning/reflection 21.21 TrueSkill); MATM shared trajectories raised ALFWorld success 47% to 55% with fewer tokens. Gap search: MATM ALFWorld 0.4708 to 0.5511 (dense) to 0.6431 (best reranker) on 274 tasks, but same-type retrieval beats cross-type (0.6314 vs 0.5985); gating by popularity beat always-retrieve by 5.3 points in Mallen 2023 (46.5% on PopQA) but only for models above about 10B. No always-retrieve vs gated test inside MATM.
agent_test: Gated retrieval of past trajectories versus none, equal tokens.

claim: Splitting load across specialists with a shared working memory helped on high-load tasks but was weak on small models and newer models that refuse to expose reasoning (CoThinker).
agent_test: Not recommended before K05-type matched-token tests pass.

claim: Team size scaling is non-monotonic; larger teams are not always better, and memory design can matter more than headcount.
agent_test: Vary memory design before agent count.

claim: The Google Stroop effect (Sparrow 2011) failed to replicate (SSRP, p=.2647 first round, .4493 pooled); the memory-for-location result was not retested in the sources read.
agent_test: Not needed for the agent.

claim: People over-use external reminders and can be trained out of it by predict-then-get-feedback (Exp 1 N=164, d=.347; Exp 2 N=416); heavy offloading to LLMs is linked to weaker recall (EEG study N=54: 83.3% of LLM group could not quote own essay versus 11.1%). Gap search: tool over-use is measured in LLM agents (Llama overuse rate above 50%; trained SMARTAgent cuts tool calls 24%), but predict-then-check feedback has no direct LLM test.
schema_part: G (agent predicts whether it needs a tool before calling it)
agent_test: Add a predict-then-check step before tool calls; measure tool calls avoided versus accuracy.

claim: Transactive memory in close couples helps only when they use their own division of memory labour; older couples show mixed collaborative inhibition.
agent_test: Not needed for the agent.

claim: The collective intelligence factor c explains about 43% of group variance in the original, but later work finds member intelligence and confidence are the strongest predictors.
agent_test: Not needed for the agent.

claim: No LLM study found directly tests Hutchins's own predictions (propagation of representational state across a system); LLM work tests architecture variants, not the DC theory.
agent_test: Inject an error in one artifact and measure whether redundant artifacts catch it.

claim: Debate is a weak operator. In tests that match calls or tokens against sampling and voting, voting equals or beats debate, and theory says plain debate leaves expected correctness unchanged (martingale). Debate gains appear only when a signal biases updates toward correct answers (oracle 0.8236 vs vanilla 0.7332; majority-conform 0.7625 vs voting 0.7691 on Qwen2.5-7B). Frontier models and external verifiers are untested.
schema_part: O (critic or debate operator); G (check against external signal)
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare self-consistency with k samples, a two-round critic, and a critic given test output; report the margin over voting.

claim: Checks work when they leave the thinker's own text. Same-model error finding is poor (GPT-4 52.87 on locating the first wrong step), repair given the location is strong, and tool-based critique beats tool-free critique. No LLM study injects errors into one of two redundant representations as Hutchins's cockpit does, so the cross-check claim stays an analogy.
agent_test: Inject known errors into a table-plus-prose pair and count catch rate for mismatch check vs same-text re-read vs test run.

claim: Whether to add agents can be pre-checked in rough form: run the single agent first (above about 45% accuracy means extra agents tend to hurt) and ask whether the subtasks are independent. The 87% held-out accuracy of Kim's model relies on trace-measured coordination metrics, so it is not a pre-run predictor.
agent_test: On 20 tasks, label sequential or parallel before running, then test whether the label predicts the sign of multi-agent minus single-agent.

claim: Shared trajectory memory helps when retrieval is relevant: MATM same-task-type retrieval beats cross-type (ALFWorld 0.6314 vs 0.5985; WebArena 0.2766 vs 0.1915). Gating beats always-retrieving in Mallen 2023 only when a good external gate exists and the model is large. Gated versus always-retrieve is untested for LLM agents with self-judged gates.
agent_test: Run agent with always-retrieve, never-retrieve, and self-gated retrieval at equal tokens on one trajectory set.

claim: Epistemic probes (search, run a test) beat pure reasoning in grounded tasks: ReAct cut hallucination as a failure cause from 56% (CoT) to 0% on HotpotQA samples and raised ALFWorld success from 45% (Act) to 71%. But tokens were not matched against deliberation, so the LLM version of the Tetris 100 ms versus 800 ms gap is not measured.
agent_test: For a fixed token budget, compare k cheap test runs against one long reasoning pass on code or puzzle tasks.
